scope: Cell-level review of page-object Table 31 /Dur and /Trans, §12.4.4.1 presentation timing, and transition-dictionary Table 164. Visual/native execution evidence is taken from the already completed transition_visual_consumer_current shard and is not recertified here.

locators: Table 31 /Dur and /Trans: physical p.121 / printed p.106 (the page-dictionary table); these entries are optional and neither is among the page-tree inheritable entries.
§12.4.4.1 presentation permission and incoming-page rule: physical p.476 / printed p.461.
Table 164 transition dictionary: physical pp.477–478 / printed pp.462–463; NOTE 2 and Figure 76 on physical p.478 / printed p.463; the clause EXAMPLE on physical p.479 / printed p.464.
effective_rules: Some interactive processors may offer presentation/slide-show mode. This implementation offers one. In that mode, optional page /Trans supplies the style and duration of the visual transition used when moving from another page to this page.

Page /Dur is a maximum display duration in seconds before automatic advance during presentation; NOTE 1 permits manual advance before expiry. The page dictionary's explicit default is no automatic advance. If /Dur is absent, no automatic advance shall occur.

Table 164 /Type is optional and, if stated, shall be Trans. /S is optional and defaults to R. R is a replacement with no special effect and the /D entry shall be ignored. Otherwise /D defaults to one second.
Dm is optional for Split/Blinds only; H means horizontal and V vertical, default H. M is optional for Split/Box/Fly only; I inward and O outward, default I.

Di is optional for Wipe/Glitter/Fly/Cover/Uncover/Push only. Numeric directions are source-defined discrete choices, with style-specific restrictions; name None is relevant only for Fly when SS is not 1.0; default is zero. EC3 #36 changes the numeric /Di type wording to integer and #75 corrects capitalization of None.

SS is optional for Fly only and defaults to 1.0; B is optional for Fly only and defaults false. Table 164 defines their meanings but does not prescribe an animation curve or every intermediate pixel. NOTE 2 assigns D to the transition into its destination page; the EXAMPLE places the transition before that page's Dur starts.
source.errata: Direct pikepdf inspection of primary physical p.478 confirms Issue #36's Caret insertions ('integer' and 'an integer') and Issue #75's 'uppercase' correction for None. The effective Table 164 text at physical pp.477–478 was read. The corrections alter table type/capitalization, not the presentation-mode condition or incoming-page timing.

limits: No universal processor obligation to offer presentation mode: the source says some interactive processors may. The project has chosen and implemented the capability, so its own enabled mode is in scope.
No requirement that every transition use a visible animation: R/default is expressly no effect. No numeric curve, frame cadence, or quantity is supplied for all styles.
Malformed Type/value rejection is not inferred from producer-side shall/if-present conditions. This review does not test invalid producer dictionaries as reader failures.

No new test draft is added because the omitted-page-Dur candidate is already promoted and passing. This review does not certify all styles on every host, all compositor/display behavior, or all sub-page navigation.
